title: Token-2022 permanent delegate
detects: A single address holding standing authority to transfer or burn any holder's balance, at any time, without that holder's consent or involvement.
knownFalseNegative: Read as transfer-restriction rather than freeze-authority because the effect on a holder is stricter than freezing: a freeze stops you moving your tokens, a permanent delegate lets someone else move them out. It is scored on the exit axis for the same reason. Note also that this cannot be added to a mint after creation, so its absence from an existing mint is durable, while its presence is not revocable by the holder.

coversExamples.observed: PRESENT, delegate 2apBGMsS6ti9RyF5TwQTDswXBWskiJP2LD4cUEDqYJjk, the same address holding every other authority on this mint
UNKNOWN by this route: a legacy Token program mint carries no extensions, so this pattern cannot look. Recorded as not looked rather than as verified absent

rationale: The most severe capability in the SPL ecosystem, and until now completely unread. The dictionary's only Token-2022 pattern matched the whole extension array to fee-control, so on a mint carrying a permanent delegate Safegate reported a fee mechanism and said nothing at all about the delegate. A reader was told the least severe true thing about the token while the most severe one was invisible.
